title: Bodycam Captures Shootout Between GRPD Officers and an 18-year-old Suspect
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Grand Rapids, Michigan — On November 11, 2025, around 1:40 p.m., in the Oakdale neighborhood of southeast Grand Rapids, near Adams Street SE and Blaine Avenue SE, two Grand Rapids police officers, a field training officer and a new recruit, were patrolling the area as part of what the chief described as “proactive police work.” They spotted an 18-year-old man who was a suspect in the theft of a firearm. Officers already knew who he was and had an “officer safety caution” issued for him, meaning police considered him potentially dangerous.

The officers parked their patrol car and got out to talk to the suspect, who was walking down the street. Dashcam and bodycam footage shows one officer calling out, “Come here, buddy, we gotta talk to you.” At first, the man kept walking away, but then he suddenly turned around and pulled out a gun, firing four shots toward the officers. The officers immediately ducked behind their cruiser for cover and returned fire, one firing seven rounds and the other firing two. Their patrol car was hit by at least one bullet, flattening a tire, and a nearby home was also struck.

Despite the exchange of gunfire, no one was hit. The suspect ran down an alley, ditching his weapon as he fled. Within ten minutes, police used drones and a perimeter search to locate and arrest him a block away. The gun was later found nearby in the grass. Both officers were placed on paid administrative leave, which is standard procedure after shootings, and the Michigan State Police took over the investigation. The suspect, who remains in custody, is expected to be charged with attempted murder and assault with intent to murder.
